This rule is part of the [nursery](/linter/#nursery) group. This means that it is experimental and the behavior can change at any time.
:::
## Summary
- Rule available since: `v2.6.8`
- Diagnostic Category: [`lint/nursery/useExpectToHaveBeenCalledTimes`](/reference/diagnostics#diagnostic-category)
- This rule has an [**unsafe**](/linter/#unsafe-fixes) fix.
- The default severity of this rule is [**information**](/reference/diagnostics#information).
- This rule belongs to the following domains:
  - [`test`](/linter/domains#test)
- Sources: 
  - Same as [`jest/prefer-to-have-been-called-times`](https://github.com/jest-community/eslint-plugin-jest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-to-have-been-called-times.md)
  - Same as [`vitest/prefer-to-have-been-called-times`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/eslint-plugin-vitest/blob/main/docs/rules/prefer-to-have-been-called-times.md)

## How to configure
```json title="biome.json"
{
	"linter": {
		"rules": {
			"nursery": {
				"useExpectToHaveBeenCalledTimes": "error"
			}
		}
	}
}

```
## Description
Enforce using `toHaveBeenCalledTimes()` to check how many times a mock function was called.

A mock function is a replacement for a real function that a test framework creates,
for example with `jest.fn()` or `vi.fn()`. It records every call it receives in its
`mock.calls` array.

Checking the length of that array with `toHaveLength()` works, but when the test fails,
the error message describes the length of an array. `toHaveBeenCalledTimes()` reports the
expected and received number of calls, which makes failures easier to understand.

The fix is unsafe because `toHaveBeenCalledTimes()` only accepts mock functions.
A value that isn't a mock function but has its own `mock.calls` array passes
`toHaveLength()` and fails `toHaveBeenCalledTimes()`.

## Examples

### Invalid

```js
expect(onSave.mock.calls).toHaveLength(1);
```

### Valid

```js
expect(onSave).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
expect(onSave).not.toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0);
expect(onSave.mock.calls[0]).toHaveLength(2);
```
